name: Software Engineering & Testing
description: How software is built in teams: process, requirements, architecture, testing at every level, code quality and delivery.

nodes.name: Software lifecycle
nodes.desc: Lifecycle models: waterfall, iterative, spiral and where each fits.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare waterfall, iterative and spiral lifecycle models and choose one that fits a project's risks.

nodes.name: Agile & Scrum
nodes.desc: Agile values, Scrum roles and ceremonies, and Kanban.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain agile values and run Scrum and Kanban practices including roles, events and boards.

nodes.name: Requirements
nodes.desc: Functional and non-functional requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria.
nodes.summary: You will be able to capture functional and non-functional requirements as user stories with clear acceptance criteria.

nodes.name: Estimation & planning
nodes.desc: Story points, estimation techniques and planning under uncertainty.
nodes.summary: You will be able to estimate work with story points and other techniques and plan releases under uncertainty.

nodes.name: Architecture styles
nodes.desc: Layered, hexagonal, event-driven and microservice architectures.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare layered, hexagonal, event-driven and microservice architectures and their trade-offs.

nodes.name: Modular design
nodes.desc: Module boundaries, interfaces and information hiding.
nodes.summary: You will be able to draw module boundaries with clean interfaces and use information hiding to contain change.

nodes.name: Docs & ADRs
nodes.desc: Design documents, architecture decision records and diagrams.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write design documents and architecture decision records and draw diagrams that communicate a design.

nodes.name: Unit testing
nodes.desc: Writing small, fast, isolated tests and the test pyramid.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write small, fast, isolated unit tests and place them correctly within the test pyramid.
topics: What makes a good unit test

nodes.name: Test case design
nodes.desc: Equivalence partitioning, boundary values and decision tables.
nodes.summary: You will be able to derive effective test cases systematically with equivalence partitioning, boundary values and decision tables.

nodes.name: Test doubles
nodes.desc: Mocks, stubs, fakes and spies and when to use them.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose between mocks, stubs, fakes and spies and use test doubles without making tests brittle.

nodes.name: TDD
nodes.desc: Red-green-refactor and letting tests drive the design.
nodes.summary: You will be able to develop code test-first using the red-green-refactor cycle and let tests shape the design.

nodes.name: Integration & E2E
nodes.desc: Integration, end-to-end and contract tests and their trade-offs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write integration, end-to-end and contract tests and balance their confidence against cost and flakiness.

nodes.name: Coverage & mutation
nodes.desc: Statement and branch coverage, and mutation testing to judge test quality.
nodes.summary: You will be able to measure statement and branch coverage and use mutation testing to judge how strong a test suite is.

nodes.name: Code review
nodes.desc: Giving and receiving review, checklists and keeping changes small.
nodes.summary: You will be able to give and receive constructive code reviews and keep changes small enough to review well.

nodes.name: Linters & analysis
nodes.desc: Linters, formatters, type checkers and static analysis tools.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use linters, formatters, type checkers and static analysis tools to catch problems before runtime.
topics: Static analysis for bugs and security
Running checks in pre-commit and CI

nodes.name: Debugging
nodes.desc: Reproducing bugs, debuggers, logging and bisecting.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find bugs systematically by reproducing them, using debuggers and logs and bisecting changes.

nodes.name: Refactoring & debt
nodes.desc: Managing technical debt and refactoring safely under tests.
nodes.summary: You will be able to identify and prioritise technical debt and pay it down through safe refactoring under tests.

nodes.name: Versioning & releases
nodes.desc: Semantic versioning, changelogs and release processes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to version software with semantic versioning, maintain changelogs and run repeatable release processes.

nodes.name: Testing in CI
nodes.desc: Running test suites automatically, flaky tests and quality gates.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run test suites automatically in CI, handle flaky tests and enforce quality gates on merges.

nodes.name: Tested library project
nodes.desc: Build a small library test-first with high branch coverage and CI.
nodes.summary: You will build a small library test-first with high branch coverage and continuous integration.

nodes.name: Team project
nodes.desc: Run a short team project with sprints, reviews and a tagged release.
nodes.summary: You will run a short team project with sprints, code reviews and a tagged release.
